title: Month 6 Day 14

items.label: Daniel & Revelation 13: The Beasts, the Ten Kingdoms & This Generation
The Abomination of Desolation: Josephus, Vespasian & the Fall of Jerusalem

notes:
This teaching begins with how to properly interpret biblical prophecy, contrasting soft and hard hermeneutics, then applies that framework to Matthew 24 and the meaning of “this generation.” It walks through Nebuchadnezzar’s statue in Daniel 2 and the four beasts of Daniel 7, connecting them to Revelation 13’s beast from the sea, the beast from the earth, and the false prophet. The study presents a first-century timeline involving the ten kingdoms, the Year of the Four Emperors, Vespasian, and the 40 years from Yeshua’s crucifixion leading toward 70 AD.

This teaching traces the First Jewish-Roman War from the revolt in 66 AD through Vespasian’s Galilee campaign and the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 AD. It closely examines Flavius Josephus—his writings, his claim that Vespasian was the promised Messiah, and his connection to the beast and false prophet—along with the roles of Vespasian and Titus. The study then focuses on the siege of Jerusalem beginning in Nisan of 70 AD, connecting Yeshua’s words in Luke 21:20-28 with the city being surrounded by armies and the Abomination of Desolation.
